A_target.statement:
Let $p$ be a [[Definition:Prime Number|prime number]] and $a \in \Z$ with $p \nmid a$.
Then:
:$a^{p - 1} \equiv 1 \pmod p$

B_source.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Finite Group|finite group]] of [[Definition:Order of Structure|order]] $n$.
Then:
:$\forall g \in G: g^n = e$

substitutions.finite group G: the multiplicative group (Z/pZ)^* of nonzero residues mod p

validity_conditions: For p prime, the nonzero residues mod p form a group under multiplication of order p-1.
The order-of-element-divides-group-order fact gives g^{|G|} = e for every g.
Instantiating with G = (Z/pZ)^* and g = a yields Fermat's little theorem.
proof_plan: The [[Definition:Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues|multiplicative group]] $\paren {\Z / p \Z}^\times$ is a [[Definition:Finite Group|finite group]] of order $p - 1$.

By [[Element to Power of Group Order is Identity]], from [[Lagrange's Theorem (Group Theory)|Lagrange's Theorem]]:
:$\forall g \in \paren {\Z / p \Z}^\times: g^{p - 1} = \eqclass 1 p$
